ops.name: abs
ops.notes: Exact decomposition: `ReLU(x) + ReLU(-x)`. Any non-zero measurement here would indicate a compiler or float32 bug.

distributions.name: abs_uniform_pm50
distributions.description: Uniform signed inputs on [-50, 50]. `abs` is exact (ReLU(x) + ReLU(-x)) so any residual is float32 round-off only.

ops.name: bool_all_true
ops.notes: Single `compare` at threshold `N-1` over the sum of N ±1 inputs. Sum is N only when all are +1; otherwise ≤ N-2 — threshold cleanly separates the two, so exact on ±1 inputs.

distributions.name: bool_triple_signed
distributions.description: Three independent ±1 boolean streams — exercises all 8 truth-table rows of `bool_any_true` and `bool_all_true`.

ops.name: bool_any_true
ops.notes: Two stacked `compare` layers. On clean ±1 inputs the intermediate sum lands well outside every ramp zone, so the composition is exact.

distributions.name: bool_triple_signed
distributions.description: Three independent ±1 boolean streams — exercises all 8 truth-table rows of `bool_any_true` and `bool_all_true`.

ops.name: bool_not
ops.notes: Single `compare` with inverted levels. Exact on clean ±1 inputs; inherits `compare`'s ramp-zone error for inputs near 0.

distributions.name: bool_single_signed
distributions.description: Random ±1 inputs (discrete, no ramp-zone samples) — `bool_not` is only defined on clean boolean inputs.

ops.name: ceil_int
ops.notes: Reduction to `-floor_int(-x)`. On integer inputs every value lands in a flat zone of the floor staircase, so the op is exact here even though it inherits approximate semantics for continuous inputs.

distributions.name: ceil_integers_neg5_10
distributions.description: Integer inputs on [-5, 10]. `ceil_int(k) = k` for integer k (flat zones in the floor staircase reused under -floor(-x)).

ops.name: clamp
ops.notes: Piecewise-linear identity with 4 breakpoints at `[lo, lo + eps, hi - eps, hi]`. In the interior flat zone (this distribution) the op is a pure identity; boundary samples would fall inside the `eps`-wide ramp and lose precision but are out of scope for this negative-control distribution.

distributions.name: clamp_flat_zone_pm20
distributions.description: Uniform samples on [-8, 8] with clamp bounds [-10, 10] — every sample is inside the flat identity zone. Residual measures float32 round-off only.

ops.name: compare
ops.notes: ReLU-pair ramp. Inputs within `1/step_sharpness` of the threshold land inside the ramp zone and yield an interpolated value; inputs further away match the step function exactly. The `compare_near_thresh_*` distributions deliberately stress the ramp — the reference is a discrete step function, so samples inside the ramp legitimately report large error.

distributions.name: compare_near_thresh_0
distributions.description: Samples within ±0.3 of the threshold at 0.0 — stresses the 2-neuron ramp zone (width 1/step_sharpness).

distributions.name: compare_uniform_pm80
distributions.description: Uniform samples on [-80, 80] — measures compare's ramp error well away from the threshold (expected ≈ 0).

ops.name: cond_gate
ops.notes: `big_offset` ReLU gate. On clean ±1 conditions the output is exactly `inp` (cond=+1) or `0` (cond=-1) up to float32 round-off; noisy conditions blur the gate.

distributions.name: cond_gate_signed_bool_times_value
distributions.description: ±1 conditions paired with scalar values in [-5, 5]. Expected output: `value` when cond=+1, `0` when cond=-1.

ops.name: equals_vector
ops.notes: Single-ReLU approximate equality test. Inside the `1/embedding_step_sharpness`-wide transition ball around the target the output interpolates between -1 and +1.

distributions.name: equals_vector_match_and_off
distributions.description: Half exact-match against target vector [1, 2, 3], half random vectors in [-3, 3]³ — measures the ReLU-based equality test's margin of separation between matches and non-matches.

ops.name: floor_int
ops.notes: Staircase with ramp width `1/step_sharpness` directly below each integer. Inputs near integer boundaries land in the ramp zone and produce interpolated values; callers with integer-ish inputs should use `thermometer_floor_div` instead, whose ramps sit at half-integer thresholds.

distributions.name: floor_near_boundary_10
distributions.description: Samples within ±1/step_sharpness of integer k=5 — stresses the ramp zone where `floor_int` interpolates.

distributions.name: floor_uniform_neg5_10
distributions.description: Uniform continuous samples on [-5, 10] — most land in flat zones; measures baseline `floor_int` accuracy.

ops.name: min
ops.notes: Exact via `(a + b - |a - b|) / 2`.

distributions.name: minmax_uniform_pm50
distributions.description: Two independent uniform streams on [-50, 50]². `min`/`max` are exact via the abs-trick; residual is float32 round-off only.

ops.name: mod_const
ops.notes: Identity `x % d = x - d · thermometer_floor_div(x, d)`. Exact on integer inputs (the input class this op is declared for).

distributions.name: mod_integers_0_100_by7
distributions.description: Integer inputs on [0, 100] with divisor=7. `mod_const` is x − divisor × `thermometer_floor_div(x)`, exact on integers.

ops.name: multiply_2d
ops.notes: Single-sublayer product built analytically via the quarter-square identity `a*b = ((a+b)^2 - (a-b)^2)/4` (O(n) neurons, no least-squares solve). Worst-cell absolute bound is `step1*step2/4 = 0.25` for this configuration.

distributions.name: multiply_uniform_pm10
distributions.description: a·b over [-10, 10]² with step=1 — generic uniform product grid; analytical bound `step1*step2/4 = 0.25`.

ops.name: multiply_integers
ops.notes: Polarization + `square` on non-negative integer inputs. Exact on integer inputs by construction (the polarization identity is exact; `square` is exact at integer grid points).

distributions.name: multiply_integers_0_10
distributions.description: Integer pairs in [0, 10] — `multiply_integers` is exact on integer inputs by construction; serves as a precision-parity check.

ops.name: piecewise_linear
ops.notes: Foundation 1D piecewise-linear primitive; measured on the canonical x² test function with 11 integer breakpoints. Error is zero at breakpoints and bounded by the interpolation error of the reference function over each segment.

distributions.name: parabola_0_10_step1
distributions.description: f(x)=x² on [0, 10] with integer breakpoints — probes generic `piecewise_linear` precision between grid points.

ops.name: reciprocal
ops.notes: Geometric breakpoint spacing keeps relative interpolation error roughly constant across the range. Measured against a reciprocal graph with `(min_value, max_value, step) = (0.3, 200.0, 1.0)`.

ops.name: square
ops.notes: Always an underestimate of x² between grid points. Max segment error is `(step/2)²` at half-integers.

distributions.name: square_unsigned_0_10
distributions.description: x² over [0, 10] with step=1.0 — exact at integers, worst error at half-integers.

ops.name: thermometer_floor_div
ops.notes: Integer-input-only staircase. Ramps sit at `k*divisor - 0.5`, giving clean separation for integer inputs. Feeding continuous floats produces ramp-zone interpolation artefacts — those belong to `floor_int`, not this op.

distributions.name: thermometer_integers_0_100_by10
distributions.description: Integer inputs on [0, 100] with divisor=10 — `thermometer_floor_div` is defined only for integer inputs.

ops.name: abs
ops.notes: `hinge(x) + hinge(-x)` = x·tanh(scale·x/2) — the rare op that regresses under swish (the relu identity is exact; |x| has a corner no smooth lane sum can express). Error is one-sided and bounded: output in [0, |x|], worst underestimate 2·swish_dip/scale (0.0056) at |x| = 1.278/scale; bit-exact for |x| ≳ 0.2 (the whole integer grid).

distributions.name: abs_near_zero_pm02
distributions.description: |x| ≤ 0.2 — the swish abs fillet zone, where the one-sided underestimate peaks (2·swish_dip/scale at |x| = 1.278/scale); the relu abs is exact here.

distributions.name: abs_uniform_pm50
distributions.description: Uniform signed inputs on [-50, 50]. `abs` is exact (ReLU(x) + ReLU(-x)) so any residual is float32 round-off only.

ops.name: bool_all_true
ops.notes: Single swiglu `compare` at threshold `N-1` over the sum of N ±1 inputs — sum is N only when all are +1, otherwise ≤ N-2. Exact to the far-field ulp class on ±1 inputs.

distributions.name: bool_triple_signed
distributions.description: Three independent ±1 boolean streams — exercises all 8 truth-table rows of `bool_any_true` and `bool_all_true`.

ops.name: bool_any_true
ops.notes: Two stacked swiglu `compare` layers. On clean ±1 inputs the intermediate sum lands well outside every ramp zone and fillet; the composition is exact to the stacked far-field ulp class (~1e-6).

distributions.name: bool_triple_signed
distributions.description: Three independent ±1 boolean streams — exercises all 8 truth-table rows of `bool_any_true` and `bool_all_true`.

ops.name: bool_not
ops.notes: Single swiglu `compare` with inverted levels — inherits compare's entry. On ±1 inputs the false side (input +1) is exact and the true side is ulp-class.

distributions.name: bool_single_signed
distributions.description: Random ±1 inputs (discrete, no ramp-zone samples) — `bool_not` is only defined on clean boolean inputs.

ops.name: broadcast_select
ops.notes: Per slot, select's complementary gated pair with mask_i as the cond — one form for every caller (the approximate flag, the (M+v)−M offsets, and the two-sublayer exact path all died). Junk-mask safe with no ±1 assert; a mask off ±1 by δ mis-scales the winner by δ·|value|. (The relu broadcast_select was never measured; its offset class is the findings doc's (M+v)−M entry.)

distributions.name: broadcast_select_pm1_masks_4x1
distributions.description: ±1 masks over 4 slots with per-slot true/false values in [-5, 5] (d_fill=1). Losing branches exactly zero at clean masks; winners ~1 ulp relative.

ops.name: ceil_int
ops.notes: −floor_int(−x); inherits floor_int's entry.

distributions.name: ceil_integers_neg5_10
distributions.description: Integer inputs on [-5, 10]. `ceil_int(k) = k` for integer k (flat zones in the floor staircase reused under -floor(-x)).

ops.name: clamp
ops.notes: piecewise_linear with 4 breakpoints, input_scale = step_sharpness; corners 0.1 apart clear the 34/K spacing audit 3x, so the only additions over relu are two isolated fillets (≤ swish_dip·|Δm|/K each).

distributions.name: clamp_flat_zone_pm20
distributions.description: Uniform samples on [-8, 8] with clamp bounds [-10, 10] — every sample is inside the flat identity zone. Residual measures float32 round-off only.

ops.name: compare
ops.notes: Sharpened-hinge ramp (`hinge(z) − hinge(z−1)`, `hinge(z) = Swish(scale·z)/scale`). Same ramp-zone contract as the ReLU form (in-ramp inputs interpolate; the near-thresh distribution deliberately stresses it). What's new vs relu: fillet dips within ~17/(scale·sharpness) of the two bends can overshoot either level by up to swish_dip/scale·|T−F| (0.0056 total span at scale=100); true-side far-field outputs carry fp32 product rounding at the lane-contribution magnitude — the same class as relu's far-field noise; the false side is exactly out_bias.

distributions.name: compare_near_thresh_0
distributions.description: Samples within ±0.3 of the threshold at 0.0 — stresses the 2-neuron ramp zone (width 1/step_sharpness).

distributions.name: compare_uniform_pm80
distributions.description: Uniform samples on [-80, 80] — measures compare's ramp error well away from the threshold (expected ≈ 0).

ops.name: cond_gate
ops.notes: One gated lane per component: `Swish(scale·cond)·inp/scale`. At clean ±1 conds the off-path is exactly zero in fp32 (σ(−scale) computes as 0.0) and the on-path passes with ~1 ulp relative rounding. No offset M, no finite-range requirement — cond noise lands as δ·|actual value|.

distributions.name: cond_gate_signed_bool_times_value
distributions.description: ±1 conditions paired with scalar values in [-5, 5]. Expected output: `value` when cond=+1, `0` when cond=-1.

ops.name: dynamic_extract
ops.notes: in_range one-hot → broadcast_select (zero-literal false branch, lanes dropped) → free Linear sum. Losing slots are exactly zero at clean masks, so the sum degenerates to a copy of the selected slot.

distributions.name: dynamic_extract_int_idx_4x2
distributions.description: Runtime 4×2 tables in [-5, 5] with integer indices — the in_range → broadcast_select → sum composition on clean integer inputs.

ops.name: equals_vector
ops.notes: One sharpened hinge on the dot-product margin. Matches are bit-exact +1; non-matches within ~17/scale past the 1/speed margin land in the hinge dip and read as low as -1 - 2·swish_dip·speed/scale (-1.0056 at scale=100) — the value-range assert carries that low-side slack. Inside the margin ball the output interpolates, as today.

distributions.name: equals_vector_match_and_off
distributions.description: Half exact-match against target vector [1, 2, 3], half random vectors in [-3, 3]³ — measures the ReLU-based equality test's margin of separation between matches and non-matches.

ops.name: floor_int
ops.notes: Two chained FFNs (bounded step, then not-yet-ON counting) — the depth is load-bearing exactly as on relu (fp32 2^24 accumulation), and the W-slack absorbs stage-1 fillet noise on ON steps the same way it absorbs fp ulps. Ramp and fillet zones near boundaries interpolate, as today; flat zones and integers are exact to the folded ulp class.

distributions.name: floor_near_boundary_10
distributions.description: Samples within ±1/step_sharpness of integer k=5 — stresses the ramp zone where `floor_int` interpolates.

distributions.name: floor_uniform_neg5_10
distributions.description: Uniform continuous samples on [-5, 10] — most land in flat zones; measures baseline `floor_int` accuracy.

ops.name: in_range
ops.notes: Per slot, two compare-shaped sharpened ramps combined in out_proj. Integer bounds are exact to the folded ulp class; continuous bounds inherit compare's ramp contract per boundary plus up to 4·swish_dip/scale ≈ 0.011 of fillet dip (the value-range assert and broadcast_select's mask tolerance both carry it). (The relu in_range was never measured.)

distributions.name: in_range_integer_bounds_8
distributions.description: Integer (lower, upper) pairs over [0, 8], 8 slots — integer bounds keep every hinge ≥ 4 units from its bend (bit-exact modulo the folded-/scale ulp class).

ops.name: map_to_table
ops.notes: Bank of equals_vector hinges rescaled to 0/1, one degenerate lane per entry, ported hinge-for-hinge. Matches read their value to ~1 ulp (the ×scale/÷scale round trip); no-match indicators underflow, so misses return the default bit-exactly. Between-keys inputs can partially fire several indicators, as today. (The relu map_to_table was never measured.)

distributions.name: map_to_table_match_and_off
distributions.description: Exact key matches (three 3-wide keys) and far-off vectors in [-1, 1]^3 — matches read their value to ~1 ulp, misses return the default bit-exactly (indicators underflow).

ops.name: min
ops.notes: `a − hinge(a−b)` plus a's sharpened bypass pair. One-sided over-estimate ≤ swish_dip/scale (0.0028), only when |a−b| ≲ 0.2; ties exact; far-apart operands carry the folded-/scale product-rounding ulp class.

distributions.name: minmax_uniform_pm50
distributions.description: Two independent uniform streams on [-50, 50]². `min`/`max` are exact via the abs-trick; residual is float32 round-off only.

ops.name: mod_const
ops.notes: x − d·thermometer_floor_div(x, d) — linear hardware plus the staircase; exact on integer inputs to the folded ulp class, as on relu.

distributions.name: mod_integers_0_100_by7
distributions.description: Integer inputs on [0, 100] with divisor=7. `mod_const` is x − divisor × `thermometer_floor_div(x)`, exact on integers.

ops.name: multiply
ops.notes: Exact ± gated-lane pair: `Swish(a)·b + Swish(-a)·(-b) = a·b` (σ(a) + σ(-a) = 1). Exact in real math at any magnitude — no grid, no range limit; measured error is fp32 rounding, relative to the actual product. Replaces the quarter-square `multiply_2d` and the `multiply_integers` chain.

distributions.name: multiply_uniform_pm10
distributions.description: a·b over [-10, 10]² with step=1 — generic uniform product grid; analytical bound `step1*step2/4 = 0.25`.

distributions.name: multiply_uniform_pm1000
distributions.description: a·b over [-1000, 1000]² — magnitudes far beyond any ReLU-era grid; probes the range-free claim of the exact gated product.

ops.name: onehot_lookup
ops.notes: Exact integer block counting: the -(n_blocks - 0.5) bias parks the winner's sharpened hinge argument at +scale/2 and everyone else's at ≤ -scale/2. Winner indicator is exactly 0.5 in fp32; losing lanes leak hinge(-0.5) ≈ -1e-22 — invisible. The tight [min, max] range claim is the reason this op exists. (The relu onehot_lookup was never measured.)

distributions.name: onehot_lookup_two_block
distributions.description: digit(3) ⊕ carry(2) one-hot pairs over all six combinations; three are table rows, three miss → default.

ops.name: piecewise_linear
ops.notes: The relu construction with sharpened hinges (K = scale·input_scale in the gate rows). Chord error between breakpoints is untouched and dominates, exactly as on relu; each corner adds a radius-17/K fillet whose dip (≤ swish_dip·|Δm|/K) bends toward the curve — grids with spacing under 34/K must raise input_scale (the spacing audit; reciprocal and the BOS inversion table do).

distributions.name: parabola_0_10_step1
distributions.description: f(x)=x² on [0, 10] with integer breakpoints — probes generic `piecewise_linear` precision between grid points.

ops.name: reciprocal
ops.notes: Geometric grid; the smallest gap (at min_value) fails the 34/K spacing audit at input_scale=1 (stacked fillets reached ~2e-2, a 20x regression), so the op derives input_scale from the smallest gap — with the fillets separated, the measured error is the chord class, as on relu.

ops.name: select
ops.notes: Complementary gated pair: `Swish(scale·cond)·a/scale + Swish(−scale·cond)·b/scale`. The losing branch contributes exactly zero at clean conds; the winner passes with ~1 ulp relative rounding. (The relu-machine select was never measured — its additive-cancellation error class, half an ulp of M, is documented in the findings doc instead.)

distributions.name: select_signed_bool_two_values
distributions.description: ±1 conditions paired with two independent branch values in [-5, 5]. Expected output: `a` when cond=+1, `b` when cond=-1.

ops.name: square
ops.notes: `multiply` with both operands the same input: `Swish(x)·x + Swish(-x)·(-x) = x²`, both terms `x²·σ(±x)` ≥ 0. Exact in real math for all x — no [0, max_value] contract, no grid, and none of the piecewise version's near-zero relative-error blowup.

distributions.name: square_uniform_pm100
distributions.description: x² over [-100, 100] — signed and wide; probes the range-free claim of the exact gated square (no [0, max_value] contract).

distributions.name: square_unsigned_0_10
distributions.description: x² over [0, 10] with step=1.0 — exact at integers, worst error at half-integers.

ops.name: table_lookup_2d
ops.notes: Both axes floor_int's two-stage staircase; the column stage is one gated lane per boundary (up row = the live row vector's adjacent difference) — the ReLU machine's mask staircase and offset-cancellation gate collapse into it, deleting the offset·0.005 guard term (the family's last range-coupled offset). On the integer grid every indicator is exactly 0/1, so the error is the delta telescoping's fp32 accumulation. (The relu table_lookup_2d was never measured; its offset-gate error class is the (M+v)−M findings entry.)

distributions.name: table_lookup_2d_int_8x6
distributions.description: Integer (i, j) over an 8×6 table with 25%% out-of-range (clamped) indices — every indicator saturated, the value path is the delta telescoping's fp32 accumulation.

ops.name: thermometer_floor_div
ops.notes: Integer-input-only staircase via piecewise_linear at input_scale = step_sharpness. Integer inputs sit in flat zones ≥ 4 units from every ramp — saturated, so exact to the folded ulp class.

distributions.name: thermometer_integers_0_100_by10
distributions.description: Integer inputs on [0, 100] with divisor=10 — `thermometer_floor_div` is defined only for integer inputs.
